climate.overview_html: Two landmark scientific assessments released this month converge on the same alarming conclusion. The Copernicus C3S July 2026 Climate Bulletin (August 10) confirmed that extra-polar ocean surface temperatures reached a new July record of 20.96°C — the joint-second warmest July globally (+1.47°C above pre-industrial average) — while Western Europe's June–July 2026 period was the hottest ever observed at +2.79°C above the 1991–2020 normal. The same day, the 36th annual BAMS State of the Climate in 2025 report — 625 scientists, 60 countries — confirmed that CO₂ hit a record 425.6 ppm, fossil fuel emissions a record 10.3 PgC/yr, and ocean heat content and global sea level also set new highs, all in a year without El Niño. That El Niño is now arriving fast: the WMO Global Seasonal Climate Update for August–October 2026 places more than 90% probability on El Niño persisting through at least November, with multi-model SST anomalies forecast to exceed 2°C. Europe's wildfire season accelerated further: JRC EFFIS reports 619,298 hectares burned as of August 19 — up 22% from the 505,683 ha as of August 5 — with very extreme fire danger forecast across Romania and Hungary through August 26 and France tracking its worst fire emissions year in 24 years.

items.headline: C3S July 2026 Bulletin: Joint-Second Warmest July on Record (+1.47°C); Extra-Polar Ocean SSTs Hit New July Record of 20.96°C; Western Europe's Hottest June–July Ever Measured
items.summary: The Copernicus Climate Change Service July 2026 climate bulletin confirms July 2026 was the joint-second warmest July globally (tied with July 2024), with an average surface air temperature of 16.90°C — 1.47°C above the estimated pre-industrial baseline. Extra-polar ocean surface temperatures reached a new July monthly record of 20.96°C, surpassing the previous July high of 20.89°C set in 2023, driven by El Niño development in the equatorial Pacific and persistent marine heatwaves in the Atlantic and western Mediterranean. Western Europe experienced its hottest June–July period on record, averaging 2.79°C above the 1991–2020 norm. CAMS fire emissions data show France's 2026 wildfire emissions tracking at or above the extreme fire years of 2022–2023 and on pace to be among the worst in 24 years. Arctic sea ice ranked sixth-lowest extent for July (most pronounced deficits in the northern Barents Sea and Svalbard); Antarctic sea ice ranked fifth-lowest. Sea surface temperatures in the equatorial Pacific continued to rise, consistent with the rapid El Niño development independently confirmed by the WMO on June 2, 2026.

items.headline: BAMS State of the Climate in 2025: Record CO₂ (425.6 ppm), Ocean Heat, Sea Level, and Fossil Fuel Emissions — 2025 Was the Warmest Year Ever Recorded Without an El Niño
items.summary: The 36th annual State of the Climate in 2025 report — compiled by 625 scientists in 60 countries and published as a special supplement to BAMS Volume 107, Issue 8 — confirms that every major climate indicator broke records in 2025 despite the absence of El Niño. Globally averaged CO₂ reached 425.6 ± 0.1 ppm (a 53% increase over the ~278 ppm pre-industrial baseline); methane and nitrous oxide also hit record concentrations. Fossil fuel emissions reached a record 10.3 ± 0.5 petagrams of carbon per year — more than three times the 1960s rate. Global ocean heat content (0–2,000 m depth) and global mean sea level each set new records. Glaciers recorded their 38th consecutive year of negative mass balance. All five major temperature datasets agree the last 11 years (2015–2025) were the 11 warmest on record; 2025 itself was the warmest year ever recorded without an active El Niño. Europe posted its warmest year on record; Russia, China, South Korea, and Argentina each recorded their second-warmest. The report explicitly flags 2026's emerging strong El Niño as a potential driver of new global temperature records.

items.headline: WMO ASO 2026 Seasonal Update: Strong El Niño Developing Rapidly — >90% Probability Through November; SST Anomalies >2°C Forecast; Positive IOD Also Emerging
items.summary: The WMO Global Seasonal Climate Update for August–October 2026 documents a rapid transition to a strong El Niño event. The multi-model ensemble projects SST anomalies exceeding 2°C in key equatorial Pacific monitoring regions (Niño-3.4, Niño-4), with the probability of El Niño persisting through at least November 2026 at or above 90% across most participating models. WMO confirmed El Niño's onset on June 2, 2026; the event has been intensifying through boreal summer. A concurrent positive Indian Ocean Dipole (IOD) is also forecast to peak during August–October, which historically amplifies drought risk across eastern Africa, parts of South Asia, and Australia during northern-hemisphere autumn. Near-universal above-normal temperatures are forecast globally for the June–August season. NOAA updated its 2026 Atlantic hurricane season outlook to 75% probability of below-normal activity — 7–13 named storms — citing El Niño-driven increases in wind shear as the primary suppressor. Phys.org coverage notes the WMO is mobilizing preparedness support across UN humanitarian agencies in anticipation of El Niño-linked disruptions to agriculture and water supply in vulnerable regions.

items.source: JRC EFFIS / Copernicus / UK Met Office
items.headline: Europe Wildfire/Drought Escalation: 619,298 ha Burned as of August 19 (Up 22% Since August 5); Very Extreme Danger Romania/Hungary Through Aug 26; UK Posts Driest July in ~200 Years of Records
items.summary: The European Forest Fire Information System reports 619,298 hectares burned across EU member states as of August 19, 2026 — a 22% increase from the 505,683 ha recorded as of August 5, which was itself 33% above the comparable 2025 rate. Very extreme fire danger conditions are forecast through August 26 across a large zone centered on Romania and Hungary, extending into the broader Balkans, Ukraine, and Russia; extreme danger also reaches southern Ireland and central-southern Italy. CAMS fire emissions data show France tracking toward its worst wildfire year in at least 24 years of records. Copernicus EDO confirms 50% of EU and UK territory is under drought at some intensity level, with 9% at alert level. CEMS has been activated more than 30 times since May 1 for wildfire emergencies across 14 European and neighboring countries. The UK Met Office separately confirmed July 2026 was the driest July in England and Wales in nearly 200 years of instrumental records, with more than half of England and all of Wales officially in drought — compounding agricultural and water-supply impacts from the preceding heatwave weeks.

major_events.name: Typhoon Saudel (WP17) — Violent Typhoon; Okinawa/Amami Direct Threat Aug 26; Super-Typhoon Before PAR Entry Aug 24
major_events.status: VIOLENT TYPHOON · ~90–115 KT · ~940 HPA · SUPER-TYPHOON INTENSITY IMMINENT
major_events.impact: As of August 23 local morning, Saudel was 2,085 km east of extreme northern Luzon with maximum sustained winds of 165–209 km/h (PAGASA 10-min / AccuWeather 1-min respectively), tracking northwest at 25 km/h. Intensity doubled from 85 kt (August 22) to violent typhoon status in under 24 hours; super-typhoon threshold (≥180 km/h) expected before PAR entry August 24. Okinawa's main island and Amami Oshima face a direct approach around August 26 with violent winds, torrential rainfall, and coastal inundation. Post-Okinawa track remains contested: KMA favors Korea, JMA tracks south of Japan's main islands, some ECMWF members target eastern China. Saudel already produced destructive 177 km/h winds at Agrihan, Northern Mariana Islands, on August 22.

major_events.name: Greece Wildfires — Multiple Active Fronts Near Athens; Salamis Island Fires Aug 16; Porto Germeno Reducing
major_events.status: ONGOING · MULTI-FRONT FIRE EMERGENCY; NEW BLAZES NEAR ATHENS OUTSKIRTS
major_events.impact: The Porto Germeno fire (started July 31, burned 10,000+ ha at peak, 2 killed in firefighter helicopter collision Aug 2) has reduced to ~2,900 ha but is not fully contained. On August 16, two new wildfires erupted on Salamis Island killing two more people. Fresh blazes have been threatening the western outskirts of Athens, triggering evacuations of Kandili, Ano Vlixada, and neighboring communities. Nearly 500 firefighters are deployed across multiple simultaneous fronts. Greece's seasonal Meltemi winds (dry northerlies, July–August) continue to drive extreme fire-spread conditions. Cause of the Porto Germeno fire traced to a faulty power-line serving a private wind farm; two individuals arrested.

major_events.name: Europe Very Extreme Fire Danger — Romania/Hungary-Centered Through Aug 26; 50% of EU in Drought
major_events.status: ONGOING · VERY EXTREME FIRE DANGER FORECAST AUG 20–26
major_events.impact: JRC EFFIS fire danger forecast shows very extreme conditions dominating a large zone centered on Romania and Hungary through August 26, extending into the broader Balkans, Ukraine, and Russia. Extreme danger conditions reach southern Ireland and central-southern Italy. Combined with 50% EU/UK drought coverage and critically low river levels (Rhine, Danube, Po, Loire), the risk of new large-scale wildfire events in central-eastern Europe is elevated. Very extreme fire danger forecast area is the largest in Europe to date in the 2026 season.

major_events.name: US South Heat Dome — Pattern Breaking Down
major_events.status: ABATING · FRONTAL PROGRESSION ACCELERATING AS OF AUG 23
major_events.impact: The 21-day heat dome event over the Gulf South — which drove heat indices of 110–115°F from Texas through the Carolinas — is in advanced breakdown as of August 23, with a frontal boundary now progressing across the Deep South. Return to near-normal temperatures is expected across the region by late this week. Residual heat risk persists through the weekend in Louisiana, Mississippi, and Alabama.

major_events.name: Atlantic Tropics — Below-Normal 2026 Season; El Niño Suppressing Development; No Active Threats
major_events.status: QUIET · NO ACTIVE TROPICAL THREATS; 75% BELOW-NORMAL SEASON PROBABILITY
major_events.impact: NOAA's August 2026 update raised the below-normal Atlantic hurricane season probability to 75%, citing rapidly intensifying El Niño increasing wind shear across the main development region. Only Arthur and Bertha have been named in 2026 to date. There are no active invests or tropical cyclones in the Atlantic basin as of August 23. Historically, every strong El Niño since 1950 has been associated with a below-normal Atlantic season.

weather.overview_html: Typhoon Saudel made a dramatic 24-hour intensity leap from 85 kt to violent typhoon status (~90–115 kt, ~940 hPa) and is now forecast to reach super-typhoon intensity before entering the Philippine Area of Responsibility on August 24. Track guidance has solidified around an Okinawa/Amami direct approach around August 26 — preparations should be well underway across the Ryukyus. In Greece, fresh blazes are erupting near Athens's western outskirts following the deadly Porto Germeno fire and the Salamis Island outbreak on August 16. JRC EFFIS's fire danger forecast shows very extreme conditions across Romania and Hungary through August 26 — the largest very-extreme-danger footprint of the 2026 Europe season to date. In the Atlantic, NOAA raised its below-normal season probability to 75% as El Niño tightens its grip; no active tropical threats exist in the basin as of August 23.

items.headline: Typhoon Saudel: Violent Typhoon as of Aug 23 — Super-Typhoon Threshold Imminent Before PAR Entry Aug 24; Okinawa/Amami Direct Threat Aug 26; Korea/Japan/China Track Contested After Okinawa
items.summary: Typhoon Saudel (WP17) escalated sharply from 85 kt / 973 mb on August 22 to violent typhoon status — approximately 90–115 kt and 940 hPa — by August 23, tracking northwest at 25 km/h at approximately 20.4°N, 143.6°E. PAGASA warns Saudel will reach super-typhoon intensity (≥180 km/h sustained) before entering the Philippine Area of Responsibility on August 24. Favorable environmental conditions — near-zero vertical wind shear, record-warm western Pacific SSTs — are driving continued rapid intensification. AccuWeather classified Saudel as a 'Violent Typhoon' with 1-minute maximum sustained winds of 209 km/h (130 mph) and gusts to 257 km/h, while PAGASA's 10-minute winds stood at 165 km/h. The storm is expected to approach Okinawa's main island and Amami Oshima around August 26 with violent winds, torrential rainfall, and dangerous coastal inundation. Saudel already produced destructive 177 km/h winds at Agrihan, Northern Mariana Islands, on August 22. Post-Okinawa track guidance diverges significantly: KMA positions landfall on the Korean Peninsula; JMA tracks the center south of Japan's main islands into the East China Sea; some ECMWF ensemble members target eastern China. Storm preparation should be underway across Okinawa, the Ryukyus, Kyushu, and the Korean Peninsula.

items.headline: Greece Wildfire Emergency: New Blazes Near Athens as Porto Germeno Wanes; Two Killed in Salamis Island Fires Aug 16 — Meltemi Winds Sustaining Multi-Front Crisis
items.summary: Greece faced an escalating multi-front wildfire emergency through August 2026. The Porto Germeno fire that broke out July 31 in Viotia — which burned more than 10,000 hectares at its peak and killed two firefighters in a helicopter collision on August 2 — has reduced to approximately 2,900 hectares; authorities traced the cause to sparks from a faulty power line serving a private wind farm and arrested two individuals. On August 16, two new wildfires erupted on Salamis Island, killing two more people, while separate blazes threatened the western outskirts of Athens, prompting evacuation orders for Kandili, Ano Vlixada, and Agios Konstantinos. Approximately 500 firefighters backed by aerial tankers have been deployed across multiple simultaneous fronts. The seasonal Meltemi winds — dry northerly flows common in July–August — continue to drive extreme fire-spread conditions across Attica and surrounding regions. Copernicus CEMS has been activated multiple times for Greece since May 2026 to provide satellite-based damage assessment and fire perimeter mapping. The Greek government approved a special tourism incentive program for Porto Germeno, Psatha, and Alepochori for the 2027 season in an effort to support local economic recovery.

items.headline: NOAA August 2026 Outlook: Below-Normal Atlantic Hurricane Season Now 75% Probable — El Niño Wind Shear Suppressing Development; Only Arthur and Bertha Named Season-to-Date
items.summary: NOAA's August 2026 Atlantic hurricane season update raised the below-normal probability to 75% (from 55% in May), cutting the named-storm forecast to 7–13 storms, 2–6 hurricanes, and 0–2 major hurricanes. The primary driver is rapid El Niño intensification: strong El Niño events increase upper-level westerly wind shear across the Atlantic main development region between the Caribbean and Africa, disrupting tropical organization before systems can intensify. Every strong El Niño event since 1950 has been associated with a below-normal Atlantic season. Through late August, only Arthur and Bertha have been named in the 2026 season. Colorado State University's August forecast, issued in parallel, also called for 9 named storms and 4 hurricanes. NOAA emphasized that below-normal probability does not eliminate hurricane risk to any individual location: 'It only takes one storm making landfall to have a catastrophic season.'

renewables.overview_html: AI-driven data center demand has emerged as the clearest structural driver of new corporate renewables contracting in 2026. RWE and Google signed a 15-year, 155 MWac PPA for the Crooked Creek Solar project in McCurtain County, Oklahoma (August 3) — RWE's first solar project in the state and its second US hyperscaler deal within a few months after a June 2026 Meta agreement in Texas. The US Energy Information Administration projects commercial electricity consumption will surpass residential for the first time in 2026, driven by AI data center load growth. In European offshore wind, Vattenfall secured both projects in Denmark's redesigned offshore wind tender (August 4) — the first contracts awarded under the revamped two-sided CfD scheme after the prior tender attracted no bids in 2024. The combined award (Hesselø 800 MW + North Sea I Mid 1 GW = 1.8 GW total, both targeting 2032 commissioning, bids of €67.42–€72.50/MWh) marks the largest Danish offshore award since the tender hiatus and a validation of the redesigned support framework. Prior digest items Sol Systems Lumberton (200 MW-ac, Texas, August 21) and AMPIN $195M green loan (100 MW India hybrid, August 20) remain this week's most recent project-finance closings.

items.headline: RWE and Google Sign 15-Year, 155 MW PPA for Crooked Creek Solar in Oklahoma — AI Data Center Demand Drives Second US Hyperscaler Deal for RWE in 2026
items.summary: RWE and Google signed a 15-year power purchase agreement covering the full output of the 155 MWac Crooked Creek Solar project in McCurtain County, Oklahoma — RWE's first solar project in the state and its second US hyperscaler PPA within a few months following a June 2026 Meta agreement in Texas. The deal was cited by both parties as a response to expanding AI data center electricity demand in the Southwest Power Pool market, which manages power delivery across 14 central and western US states. Construction is scheduled to begin in 2026 with commissioning targeted for 2028. The project is expected to create up to 250 peak construction jobs, generate approximately $24.3 million in local economic activity during construction, and contribute an estimated $25 million in long-term county revenue. RWE also operates the 148 MW Boiling Springs Wind project in Woodward County, Oklahoma, and has six additional projects totaling 1.6 GW in development across the state. The US EIA expects commercial electricity consumption to surpass residential for the first time ever in 2026, driven by AI data center load growth — a structural shift that is pulling new utility-scale solar projects toward completion ahead of schedule.

items.headline: Vattenfall Wins Both Projects in Denmark's Redesigned Offshore Wind Tender: Hesselø (800 MW) + North Sea I Mid (1 GW) = 1.8 GW Combined, Operational by 2032
items.summary: Vattenfall was awarded both projects in Denmark's first successful offshore wind tender under the redesigned two-sided Contract for Difference (CfD) framework introduced after the country's prior 3 GW tender attracted no bids in late 2024. Hesselø (800 MW minimum, Kattegat Sea, approximately 30 km from the coast) and North Sea I Mid (1 GW minimum, near Hvide Sande, approximately 20 km from the coast) together represent at least 1.8 GW of new capacity expected fully operational by 2032 — enough to supply approximately 1.8 million households. Vattenfall submitted winning bids of €72.50/MWh for Hesselø and €67.42/MWh for North Sea I Mid — the lowest bids at each location — and will receive the offered price for 20 years from commissioning. The Danish Energy Agency's revised tender, launched November 2025, offered two-sided CfDs with state aid and extended project timelines versus the prior design. A third site — Nordsøen Syd (1 GW) — remains open for bids through October 2028. Vattenfall currently operates five Danish offshore wind farms generating ~6.5 TWh/year. The award signals that the redesigned CfD scheme has restored investor appetite for Danish offshore wind after the 2024 collapse.

science.overview_html: The 36th annual BAMS State of the Climate in 2025 (625 scientists, 60 countries, BAMS Vol. 107, No. 8) and the joint Copernicus Marine / C3S release on daily SST records together frame this week's science output: every major climate indicator tracked record-breaking trajectory in 2025 and into summer 2026, with the world's oceans now repeatedly breaching daily temperature records for the time of year as El Niño intensifies. On the AI-weather front, WindBorne's WeatherMesh-6 — announced alongside the company's $37M Series B — claims the top position on publicly available accuracy benchmarks while using substantially less compute than traditional NWP, and its 600+ long-duration balloons are now assimilated into NOAA's Global Forecast System. A timely perspective paper by Dueben, Bauer, Fuhrer, Koldunov, and Kristiansen (arXiv:2606.25076, June 2026) argues the next frontier for ML-based NWP is not accuracy — where the battle is effectively won — but an organizational and cultural transformation of how meteorologists, observation system designers, and forecast centers restructure workflows around the data-driven paradigm.

items.headline: State of the Climate in 2025 (BAMS Vol. 107 No. 8): CO₂ 425.6 ppm Record, 38th Consecutive Year of Glacier Mass Loss, Warmest Non-El-Niño Year Ever — 2026 El Niño Could Push to New Extremes
items.summary: The 36th annual State of the Climate report compiled by 625 scientists in 60 countries confirms 2025 broke records for CO₂ concentration (425.6 ppm, 53% above pre-industrial), fossil fuel emissions (10.3 PgC/yr, more than three times the 1960s rate), global ocean heat content (0–2,000 m), and global mean sea level — all in a year without El Niño. The 11 warmest years on record all occurred in the past 11 years. Glaciers recorded their 38th consecutive year of negative mass balance. The report highlights that 2025 exceeded the typical ENSO-neutral baseline by a substantial margin, reflecting the accumulated background warming signal. The authors note that with a strong El Niño now developing in 2026, 2026 or 2027 could produce new global temperature records. Published in BAMS Volume 107, Issue 8 (August 2026) and freely available online through the AMS journals platform.

items.headline: Copernicus: Daily Global SSTs Repeatedly Breaking Records for Time of Year Through July–August 2026 — Extra-Polar Monthly Average Reaches New July Record of 20.96°C
items.summary: A joint release from the Copernicus Marine Service and the Copernicus Climate Change Service documents that daily global average sea surface temperatures have repeatedly broken records for the time of year through the July–August 2026 window, consistent with the rapid development of El Niño in the equatorial Pacific and persistent anomalous warmth in the North Atlantic and Mediterranean. The extra-polar monthly-average SST for July 2026 reached 20.96°C — a new July record, surpassing the previous high of 20.89°C set in July 2023. SST anomalies in the Atlantic coast waters and western Mediterranean have been associated with severe marine heatwaves fueling both extreme wildfire-conducive conditions inland and enhanced tropical cyclone intensification potential. The joint release emphasizes that while part of the SST signal is driven by El Niño's contribution, the persistence of above-normal temperatures outside the equatorial Pacific region reflects the long-term background warming trend rather than ENSO variability alone.

items.headline: WeatherMesh-6: WindBorne Claims World's Most Accurate Weather Forecasting Model on Public Benchmarks — 600+ Long-Duration Balloons Now Assimilated Into NOAA GFS
items.summary: WindBorne Systems announced that its WeatherMesh-6 model ranks as the world's most accurate weather forecasting model based on publicly available benchmarks while requiring substantially less compute to train than traditional NWP approaches. The company, which operates more than 600 autonomous long-duration sensing balloons simultaneously, tripled the size of its global balloon network over the past year while tripling revenue. WindBorne's balloon-based atmospheric observations are now assimilated into NOAA's Global Forecast System (GFS), one of the world's foundational public forecasting systems. The company frames its infrastructure as providing observations in regions historically poorly sampled by radiosondes and aircraft — particularly over remote ocean areas — where data-sparse gaps most degrade ML model accuracy. The WeatherMesh-6 performance claim is tied to the company's $37M Series B announcement (see Industry). The TechCrunch profile raises the broader commercial question of whether superior accuracy alone can build a durable business model in weather forecasting or whether value capture requires vertical integration into specific industries such as energy, agriculture, or reinsurance.

items.source: ECMWF / NCEP / Environment and Climate Change Canada / arXiv
items.headline: Dueben, Bauer et al.: Machine Learning Is Revolutionizing Weather Forecasting — The Next Step Is a Change in How We Work (arXiv:2606.25076)
items.meta: Peter Dueben, Peter Bauer, Oliver Fuhrer, Nikolay Koldunov, Jørn Kristiansen · arXiv:2606.25076 · physics.ao-ph / cs.CY
items.summary: Senior researchers from ECMWF (Dueben, Bauer), CSCS (Fuhrer), Alfred Wegener Institute (Koldunov), and the Norwegian Meteorological Institute (Kristiansen) argue in this June 2026 perspective paper that the ML-versus-NWP accuracy debate is effectively over: leading AI models now match or exceed traditional forecast skill across most metrics while running thousands of times faster. The central argument is that the field now faces a second, less-discussed transformation — organizational and cultural — that goes beyond model architecture. The authors contend that maximizing the value of ML-based NWP requires restructuring workflows, observation design, data assimilation pipelines, and forecast post-processing around the data-driven paradigm, rather than grafting ML components onto legacy NWP frameworks. They identify collaboration models, talent pipelines, and the role of national meteorological institutes as the key constraints now limiting progress — not algorithmic capability. The paper directly engages the 'hybrid' model debate, arguing that the field should clarify what 'hybrid' means (ML-corrected NWP vs. physics-informed ML vs. coupled systems) and design evaluation frameworks accordingly.

items.title: WindBorne Systems Closes $37M Series B — Khosla Ventures and Galvanize Co-Lead Round for Weather Balloon and AI Forecasting Platform; Valuation $250M
items.body_html: WindBorne Systems closed a $37 million Series B co-led by Khosla Ventures and Galvanize on August 5, 2026, with additional participation from Translink Capital, Lux Capital, and existing investors, valuing the company at $250 million post-money. Total equity funding raised to date exceeds $62 million. The Redwood City, California company operates more than 600 autonomous long-duration sensing balloons simultaneously — the world's longest-flying weather balloon fleet — and tripled both its network size and revenue over the past year. Its WeatherMesh-6 model claims the top position on publicly available accuracy benchmarks while requiring substantially less compute than legacy NWP; observations are now assimilated into NOAA's Global Forecast System (GFS). Proceeds will expand the balloon constellation, increase compute access, and develop next-generation WeatherMesh models and enterprise weather intelligence products. CEO John Dean described the vision as building 'a planetary nervous system that continuously observes Earth's atmosphere' — with value capture flowing into energy, transportation, agriculture, and emergency response verticals.

items.title: Currence (CTVC) H1 2026 Climate Tech Report: $26.1B Raised — Up 55% YoY — as AI Data Centers Drive Surge; Deal Count Down 25%; Series C Up Fourfold
items.body_html: The H1 2026 Climate Tech Investment & Innovation Report from Currence (publisher of the CTVC newsletter) finds that venture capital investment in climate technology reached $26.1 billion in the first half of 2026 — up 55% year-on-year and the strongest first-half for the sector since 2022. But the headline growth masks a sharp concentration dynamic: total deal count fell 25% even as total capital surged, with 34% of all climate tech funding going to low-carbon data center technologies — a category that represented just 3% of funding a year earlier. ESG Today highlights that two data center deals alone — DayOne ($4.5B Series C) and Nscale ($2B Series C) — accounted for nearly two-thirds of all Series C funding in the half. Series C funding overall reached $10.5 billion, up nearly fourfold from H1 2025. Other large H1 deals included Fervo Energy's $1.9B IPO (geothermal) and X-Energy's $1B IPO (advanced nuclear). Currence attributes the pattern to what it calls the speed-to-power race: with gas turbine lead times stretching into multi-year backlogs, AI infrastructure developers are pulling forward low-carbon generation assets that can be brought online faster.
